fullPassage:
(A) "Mia, let's go walk our dog!" Julia called out, but there was no answer. She checked her daughter's room and found that Mia was absorbed in her smartphone, wearing her earbuds. Julia was concerned about her daughter. She turned to her husband, Sam. "Mia seems to live inside her phone, not with us." Sam nodded, "I know. I feel like she is growing distant from us. Why don't we set up a family reading club?" Julia brightened at the suggestion, and Sam promised to talk with Mia about it.

(B) Mia's family held their first book club meeting on Saturday afternoon. Everyone enjoyed the book Mia had chosen. Julia was the first to speak: "Dr. Duvall nearly invented a drug for eternal life, yet disappeared one day and ended up running Café Paris. That's such a mystery." Mia responded, her eyes sparkling, "Mom, I understand him. He always dreamed of being a barista, and his dream came true." Sam supported his daughter, and their conversation grew lively. During the discussion, Mia felt reconnected with her parents and already looked forward to their next book club meeting.

(C) At the library, Mia scanned the shelves for nearly an hour, feeling lost among the endless titles. Then, a librarian approached and asked, "Looking for something in particular?" "I need a book for my family's reading club," Mia admitted. "What genre do you enjoy?" she asked kindly. "Hmm, I like mysteries," Mia replied. The librarian handed her a book titled Café Paris and said with a smile, "You'll love this one." Mia thanked her and checked it out.

(D) When Sam suggested starting a family reading club, Mia immediately shook her head and said, "No, Dad. I don't have time to read books. You know how busy I am with exams all semester." He didn't give up. "But wouldn't it be fun if we all read the same story and shared our thoughts? You could simply read for 20 minutes, maybe during your lunch break." After some persuasion, Mia reluctantly agreed. Deep down, she knew she was spending too much time on her phone. So she asked, "Dad, can I choose the first book?" Sam gladly said, "Yes."

questions.passage: (A) Julia checked her daughter's room and found that Mia was (A) __________ in her smartphone. Julia was (B) __________ about her daughter. Sam said, "I feel like she is growing (C) __________ from us."

det.analysis:
✅①: absorbed — concerned — distant = 원문과 일치
❌②: distracted는 absorbed의 유사어이나 원문과 다름
❌③: worried는 concerned의 유사어이나 (A)가 다름
❌④: (C) close는 distant의 반의어

questions.passage: (B) Everyone enjoyed the book Mia had chosen. Julia was the first to <u>speak</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 speak가 이 글에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 문맥에서의 의미는 (의견을) 발언하다이다. 다의어는 문맥에 따라 뜻이 달라진다.
det.analysis:
❌① (언어를) 구사하다: 다른 문맥에서의 의미
❌② (전화로) 통화하다: 다른 문맥에서의 의미
✅③ (의견을) 발언하다: 독서 토론에서 처음으로 말한 것
❌④ (연설을) 하다: 다른 문맥에서의 의미
det.tip: 다의어 — 같은 단어도 문맥에 따라 뜻이 달라집니다. 앞뒤 문맥을 꼼꼼히 읽으세요.

questions.passage: (C) Mia thanked her and <u>checked</u> it out.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 checked가 이 글에서 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 문맥에서의 의미는 (도서를) 대출하다이다. 도서관에서 check out = 대출하다.
det.analysis:
❌① (사실을) 확인하다: 다른 문맥에서의 의미
❌② (호텔을) 체크아웃하다: 다른 문맥에서의 의미
✅③ (도서를) 대출하다: 도서관에서 checked it out
❌④ (시험을) 검사하다: 다른 문맥에서의 의미
det.tip: 다의어 — check out은 도서관에서 '대출하다'의 뜻으로 쓰입니다.

det.korean: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 genre가 가장 적절하다. 도서관에서 어떤 종류(장르)를 좋아하는지 묻는 맥락.

❌③ topic: 주제 — 장르가 더 적합
❌④ format: 형식 — 문맥에 맞지 않음
